sw_landlord.text: Fàilte! Welcome to the Minch Arms. If you're wanting a quiz, Scottish questions, losers buy the crisps. If you're wanting a pint, be prepared to wait. The queue's a long one and the tap is a slow one.

then.text: Go well. And remember: in the Gaelic tradition a verse is a gift. Answer a Blue Man's verse with a good one, and he'll give you a gift back.
The Skipper sent you? About the Blue Men? Right. A rhyme has two halves. The Blue Man gives you the first. You answer in the same tune, ending on the same sound. If it ends well, it holds.
Test: if he says 'tide', you say...
Ride! Exactly. 'Tide' and 'ride'. Tide-wide-ride-guide. Easy as that. You've the ear. Away and catch a gale.

else.text: No, no. Listen to the ending. 'Tide'. Now think of something you do on a horse. Try again.
I'm the Bard of Stornoway. Mostly of the Minch Arms. I wrote a song about the weather and it's got forty verses. It's about the same weather, but I think of it as an epic.
